Listen to this article Share Enugu Electricity Distribution Company PLC (EEDC) has deployed a digital platform to enable electricity customers across the South East states who subscribed to the Meter Asset Provider (MAP) scheme to conveniently access and monitor their meter refund tokens. Advertisement Advertisement The initiative is part of the company’s efforts to improve customer experience, promote transparency, and ensure that customers who paid for metres under the MAP scheme can track and access their refunds. The MAP initiative, introduced by the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) as part of efforts to bridge the metering gap in the Nigerian electricity sector, provides an avenue for electricity customers without meters to acquire it at their own cost, with the distribution companies reimbursing them with the cost of the meter through energy credits as they recharge their meters. Consequently, EEDC has provided a digital channel through which eligible customers can retrieve their refund tokens at the comfort of their homes. To access the service, customers are required to send “Hi,” “Hello,” or “100” to WhatsApp number, +234 815 082 4825. Upon initiating the conversation, a menu of available services will appear. Customers should select the “MAP Refund Token” option and provide their meter number to retrieve their refund token. Advertisement Alternatively, customers can access the platform directly through the dedicated web portal: https://maprefund.myeedc.com/ The platform is expected to make the refund process more accessible, convenient, and transparent while empowering customers to independently monitor their MAP refund entitlements. Advertisement Emeka Ezeh, the Group Head, Corporate Communications, EEDC, in a statement issued on Tuesday, said that the deployment of the platform underscores the company’s commitment to leveraging technology to enhance service delivery and strengthen its engagement with customers. He encouraged all customers who acquired meters under the MAP scheme to take advantage of the platform to access their refund information and tokens. Advertisement Advertisement According to him, this also applies to customers of all the subsidiary distribution companies that are under the EEDC HoldCo, which includes MainPower, TransPower, FirstPower, NewEra, and EastLand. Ezeh further urged customers to utilise the designated WhatsApp channel or web portal for the service and to ensure that they provide the correct meter numbers. He reiterated EEDC’s commitment to continuously introducing innovative solutions that address customers’ needs, improve operational efficiency, and deliver a better electricity service experience.
